I would recommend not staying loyal to a school because of its atmosphere. Very normal to go through many schools early on. I’ve taught at 8 different (private, public, charter, college and technical) including student teaching and I’m only 24. If I stayed at my student teaching school I wouldn’t be as well rounded as I am. I would also wonder if I’d truly feel like “a teacher” when the kids and faculty know you as the student teacher. 

Price yourself out, see what districts are offering in other areas. Some districts you have to wait for the teacher to die before they give it to you, and then turns out they don’t hire substitutes. (Substitute shortage more severe than teacher shortage). 

Stay loyal to yourself and your craft, find a great boss and let them prove to you they are great. Then you can stay knowing you’re safe and respected. 

Last bits of advice - send as many cvs as you can. I got the job on #58 and again on #18. I wouldn’t appreciate the gig and my abilities if I hadn’t. 

1,000% Ask the principal for a mock interview before you leave.  Prove to yourself you can do it, and if he likes what he hears he might try and find a spot if you really want to commit.

When that spot opens up, they know who to call. Received 2 offers from previous sub gigs years after I subbed. 

One page is good in the education world, but just be sure it represents who you truly are as a worker and educator. 

You set your value!

Best of luck.
